symbols.name: factor bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers given to the established multiplier.
symbols.quote: The established multiplier is the earlier Harvey–van der Hoeven algorithm, which multiplies two integers of $N$ bits each in $O(N\log N)$ time (this $N$ is not the bank size of the exchange network); the new algorithm calls it as an ordinary subroutine for the integer products it cannot avoid.

relations.quote: The multiplier runs in the [Fixed finite-tape machine model](machine-model.md), the same model as the main result, so a call costs its $O(N\log N)$ steps with no change of machine to account for.

relations.predicate: is called on products from reducing
relations.quote: The first kind arises once the new algorithm reduces its [Fourier transforms](dft.md) to polynomial products over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$.
